clinicalPearls: A chromosomal disorder affecting females caused by complete or partial absence of one X chromosome, most commonly a 45,X karyotype, with mosaic forms also occurring.
The two most consistent features are short stature and gonadal dysgenesis leading to ovarian failure.
Newborns may show puffiness of the hands and feet (lymphoedema) and redundant nuchal skin; a fetal cystic hygroma may be detected antenatally.
Characteristic features can include a webbed neck, low posterior hairline, widely spaced nipples on a broad chest, and a wide carrying angle at the elbows.
Congenital cardiovascular anomalies, particularly bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation of the aorta, carry a risk of aortic dilatation and dissection and require ongoing surveillance.
Renal anomalies such as a horseshoe kidney are common, as are recurrent otitis media and hearing loss.
Most girls have normal intelligence but may have specific difficulties with visuospatial and mathematical tasks.
Growth hormone therapy is used to improve final height, and oestrogen replacement is used to induce puberty and maintain bone and uterine health.
Diagnosis is confirmed by karyotype, and lifelong multidisciplinary follow-up addresses cardiac, endocrine, and reproductive needs.
reference.pathophysiology: Loss of all or part of the second sex chromosome causes haploinsufficiency of genes that normally escape X-inactivation and are needed in two copies. Deficiency of the SHOX gene contributes to short stature and skeletal features, while accelerated loss of ovarian follicles leads to gonadal dysgenesis and oestrogen deficiency. Abnormal fetal lymphatic development produces the lymphoedema, nuchal changes, and associated features such as the webbed neck, and disrupted development contributes to the cardiovascular and renal malformations.
additionalDifferentials: Noonan syndrome (overlapping webbed neck and short stature, normal karyotype)
Other causes of short stature (growth hormone deficiency, constitutional delay)
Other causes of primary ovarian insufficiency or delayed puberty
additionalInvestigations: Karyotype to confirm monosomy X or mosaicism (with additional cells if mosaicism suspected)
Echocardiography and cardiac MRI to assess aortic valve, arch, and aortic dimensions
Gonadotrophins (FSH, LH) and thyroid function testing
Bone age and growth monitoring; screening for coeliac disease
redFlags: Aortic dilatation or symptoms suggesting aortic dissection
Severe coarctation or critical cardiac lesions in infancy
Features suggesting Y-chromosome material, which raises gonadoblastoma risk
Signs of untreated hypothyroidism or coeliac disease
reference.prognosis: With appropriate hormone therapy and surveillance most girls achieve improved height, undergo induced puberty, and have a good quality of life; long-term outlook is influenced chiefly by cardiovascular complications, and fertility is usually impaired though assisted reproduction may be possible.
pitfalls: Not considering the diagnosis in a girl with unexplained short stature or delayed puberty
Missing mosaicism when only a limited number of cells are analysed
Overlooking the need for lifelong aortic surveillance
Failing to screen for associated hypothyroidism, coeliac disease, and hearing loss
management: Recombinant growth hormone therapy in childhood to improve final adult height, with oxandrolone as a possible adjunct
Oestrogen replacement to induce puberty followed by maintenance combined oestrogen-progesterone hormone therapy for gonadal failure
Lifelong cardiovascular surveillance with echocardiography and aortic MRI for bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation and aortic dilatation or dissection risk
Monitoring and management of associated conditions including renal anomalies, hypothyroidism, coeliac disease, recurrent otitis media, hearing loss and reduced bone density
Fertility counselling with assisted reproduction via oocyte donation and pre-pregnancy cardiac assessment given dissection risk
Urgent evaluation for acute aortic dissection in any patient presenting with acute chest pain
Multidisciplinary care with karyotype confirmation and genetic counselling
